title: 急に — “suddenly”
summary: 急に is an adverb meaning “suddenly, abruptly.” It describes a change or event that happens quickly and without warning, and goes before a verb. It is used for both pleasant and unpleasant surprises.

patterns.form: 急に ＋ 動詞（変化・出来事）
patterns.gloss: 急に変わる / 急に呼ばれる / 急に用事ができる

body.p: It is the に form of the na-adjective 急だ, used as an adverb. It shares a kanji with 急ぐ, but 急に means “suddenly,” not “quickly.”
Use it when weather, feelings or plans change unexpectedly: 急に天気が変わりました, 急に用事ができて、行けなくなった. With the passive (呼ばれた) the feeling of surprise is stronger.
突然 is a little more formal and common in writing. いきなり is more casual and stronger in surprise. 急に sits between the two and fits either.

examples.ja: 急（きゅう）に天気（てんき）が変（か）わりました。
駅（えき）で急（きゅう）に名前（なまえ）を呼（よ）ばれた。
examples.romaji: Eki de kyū ni namae o yobareta.
examples.tr: At the station, I was suddenly called by name.

examples.ja: 急（きゅう）に用事（ようじ）ができて、行（い）けなくなった。
examples.romaji: Kyū ni yōji ga dekite, ikenaku natta.
examples.tr: Something suddenly came up, so I couldn't go.

pitfalls: 急に does not mean “quickly.” Do not confuse it with 急いで (急いで走る).
Do not drop the に: 急天気が変わった is wrong.
